problem: The pipeline is written with head -2 (and Q3 with head -1). head -2 is a GNU/BSD convenience form; POSIX head only guarantees -n, and the chapter itself stresses POSIX-portable scripts and teaches the -n form in Section 2. A student copying this onto a strict POSIX system may get an error.
fix: Use head -n 2 in the worked example, the figure spec and the dry run, and head -n 1 in Q3, so the form matches the -n usage taught in Section 2.

problem: The text says the pipe starts two processes but never says they run at the same time, connected by a kernel buffer. A student can easily read it as "left command finishes, then right command starts", which is wrong and makes later points (head exiting early, large streams) hard to understand.
fix: Add one sentence: the shell starts both commands at once; the left writes into a buffer in the kernel and the right reads from it as data arrives, so neither waits for the other to finish.

problem: PIPESTATUS is described as holding every stage's status, but not that it is overwritten by the very next command run. A student who writes a pipeline and then an echo before reading ${PIPESTATUS[0]} will read the wrong value.
fix: Add: copy it immediately after the pipeline, for example st=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}"), because any following command replaces the array.
